newsitem.title: USA: Doubletree to buy Renaissance Hotel.
newsitem.headline: Doubletree to buy Renaissance Hotel.

text.p: Hotel operator Doubletree Corp has agreed to buy Renaissance Hotel Group NV in a stock and cash transaction valued at $850 million, including the assumption of $70 million of debt, the companies said Tuesday.
Under terms of the deal, Doubletree will pay $8 cash and 0.4105 share of Doubletree common for each Renaissance share, they said.
The deal values Renaissance shares at $25.30 each, based on the current value of Doubletree stock, the companies said.
The exchange ratio of 0.4105 Doubletree share for each Renaissance share will not change, the companies said.
Renaissance's majority owner, New World Group, has agreed to tender its 54.4 percent of Renaissance shares and vote in favor of the transaction, the companies said.
The companies have agreed to a $50 million break-up fee, to be paid by the party failing to proceed with the merger.
The companies said they expect to execute a memorandum of understanding within two days.
The merger requires regulatory approval and approval by the boards of both companies, they said.
Doubletree and Renaissance officials were not available for further comment.

Renaissance is a Netherlands-based hotel manager, with 138 hotels under management or franchise pacts. The company's ADRs were up 7-7/8 to 24-1/4 on the New York Stock Exchange about 90 minutes after the merger announcement.
Doubletree's stock was off 1-5/8 to 45-7/8. Doubletree has 236 properties, either owned or under lease or management contract.
Doubletree also announced today that Anupam Narayan had been named senior vice president and treasurer.
Most recently, Narayan served as vice president and treasurer of Red Lion Hotels Inc until the merger between Doubletree and Red Lion became effective in November.
